implemented: Added deterministic configuration content revisions without changing the legacy schema_version=1 project.json shape; init, assembly show/edit and operation results expose the revision used.

Added bounded project configuration history (20 prior snapshots), written through an atomic sidecar update and revision-checked updates. Stale writes return a structured PROJECT_CONFIG_CONFLICT and retain the newer workspace configuration.

Added source-aware input resolution for explicit CLI values, saved run/variant values, workbench session candidates, project defaults and product defaults. Direct operations annotate model/batch/binding provenance; run records preserve config revision and input source lineage across try repeat and resume.

Added per-operation readiness plans to assembly show. Model inspect is ready without batch or training configuration; forward readiness identifies the example-batch action and does not require unrelated optimizer/loss fields.
Added tests for precedence, scoped revision identity, readiness states, legacy config compatibility, config history/stale revisions, explicit overrides and saved-run provenance.

Added human assembly-show readiness and provenance summary: operation state, base configuration revision, input requiredness/state/source/reference, capability and fact reasons, and suggested actions; resolved input values are never rendered.

Added `m-model config history` and a selected-field `config restore` command; restore previews by default, validates historical content revisions, rejects ambiguous prefixes and unsupported fields, and uses revision-checked writes when `--apply` is explicit.

Added a project configuration/history destination to the human workbench; users can select a prior version, choose fields, inspect the preview, and confirm before writing. The pre-restore current config is retained in bounded history.
Added a shared human-mode input provenance summary for model, try, train and edit reports. It shows each resolved input source, reference and scoped revision without echoing resolved values.

Added operation-specific input readiness preflight for model inspect/probe/verify, try/train, and Layer query/edit commands. Missing required entries return a structured plan and do not start the execution worker; JSON plans redact resolved input values.

Human terminal output renders readiness state, required input status and provenance, known facts/capabilities, and actionable next steps. Invalid config, stale replay, and operations whose requirements are owned by their concrete service continue through to authoritative application diagnostics.
External-loop readiness now treats the user loop as required while model and batch inputs remain optional, matching the operation contract.

Operation-complete plans now query the selected Python Worker doctor capability catalog and report actual supported/unsupported/unknown feature states with providers and reasons. The catalog is cached for the application session and invalidated when the interactive Python runtime changes.

A required capability reported unsupported blocks only the selected target operation with OPERATION_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. Unknown capability status remains visible and does not claim readiness or silently block an operation that the runtime can still validate.

Plans with missing required inputs do not start a Worker solely for capability detection; uncached capabilities remain optional/unknown until inputs are complete. Human prompts now derive from plan-required missing fields, so saved defaults are not redundantly prompted and external-loop does not ask for an independent model or batch.

Capability checks use the selected Backend runtime through doctor, retain the validated catalog for the application session, and invalidate it when the interactive Python runtime is changed. Unsupported required features produce OPERATION_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE before target dispatch; unknown runtime status is reported without claiming ready.

Capability-check interruption now returns USER_INTERRUPTED and stops the target operation. The main CLI keeps SIGINT handling active between sequential Worker calls so Ctrl+C during the Doctor/operation boundary is not swallowed.

Interactive prompts are now driven by the same operation readiness plan as JSON/CLI execution. They prompt only for missing required inputs, respect project defaults and saved replay inputs, and external-loop does not ask for model/batch inputs.

扩展操作级 readiness：组件 show/check/test 显示描述、依赖、参数、fixture 与 Worker conformance 能力；Layer 编辑计划区分 plan_layer_edit/apply_layer_edit，并记录选区和持久化目标。注册 Provider 编辑还预检 kind、layer_edit 声明、依赖、fixture 和符合性记录；无法静态确认的 payload/源码/运行时绑定仍交由 Worker 执行时复核。静态阻塞保留组件领域诊断码和原因。

将 Operation Plan contract 升至 v2；CapabilityAvailability.conditional 与 unknown 在 readiness facts/capabilities 中分别序列化，并为 required conditional 状态保留条件说明。终端状态使用“有条件”，同步 operations JSON Schema 与 module interface 文档。
为 Provider Layer 编辑计划计算整数/字符串 payload 的 Worker 兼容摘要，准确区分没有对应 payload 验证记录（missing）和存在记录但仍须在执行时复核源码/Python/PyTorch（conditional）；浮点 payload 摘要保留为运行时条件，避免 Rust/Python 浮点格式差异造成错误拦截。

Provider verification failures now include structured mismatch fields and recorded/current Python version, PyTorch version, payload digest and provider/fixture source fingerprints. Human diagnostics show those exact mismatches; static readiness remains conditional where Python/PyTorch execution facts cannot be known in Rust.
